title: finding(fields): `deriveLookupColumns` is exported from the package root but its `objectSchema` parameter type is a third unexported `ObjectSchemaLike`
body:
Found while implementing objectui#7324 (the same defect in `@object-ui/plugin-form`). Filed rather than fixed: `packages/fields` is outside that card's package, and its shape is a **third** distinct type, so folding it in would have made #7324's own surface decision harder to review, not easier.

## The gap

`packages/fields/src/widgets/deriveLookupColumns.ts:65` exports:

```
export function deriveLookupColumns(
  objectSchema: ObjectSchemaLike | null | undefined,
  { displayField, max = 4 }: DeriveColumnsOptions,
): LookupColumnDef[]
```

and `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:3210` carries it to the package root with `export * from './widgets/deriveLookupColumns.js';` (present in the built root surface, `packages/fields/dist/index.d.ts:722`).

Its first parameter type is declared at `:21` with **no `export` keyword**:

```
interface ObjectSchemaLike {
  fields?: Record<string, { type?: string; label?: string; hidden?: boolean; system?: boolean }>;
  highlightFields?: unknown;
  displayFields?: unknown;
}
```

`export *` does not carry a module-private declaration, so the name never reaches the root. `DeriveColumnsOptions` — the OTHER parameter type on the same signature — **is** exported. `ObjectSchemaLike` is the one that is not. Same asymmetry, same consequence: a consumer of `deriveLookupColumns` cannot name what it must pass, so it restates a producer-owned shape by hand, and the restatement is invisible to every gate until the producer's shape moves.

## What makes this its own card rather than part of objectui#7324

It is a **third** structurally distinct shape carrying the name `ObjectSchemaLike` in this repo, and it is not interchangeable with either of the two in `plugin-form`:

| declaration | `fields` value type | other members |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.ts` (now `ChildObjectSchemaLike`) | `any` | `name?` |
| `plugin-form/src/schemaDefaults.ts` (now `FieldDefaultsSchemaLike`) | `{ defaultValue?, type?, reference?, reference_to? }` | — |
| `fields/src/widgets/deriveLookupColumns.ts` (this one) | `{ type?: string; label?: string; hidden?: boolean; system?: boolean }` | `highlightFields?`, `displayFields?` |

Note this one pins `type` and `label` to `string`, where the `plugin-form` defaults shape leaves `type` as `unknown` — so it is not a subtype of either. Whoever takes this should run the same structural comparison objectui#7324 ran before choosing a name, and should NOT reuse a name that already means something else in a sibling package a consumer may import alongside this one.

## Options

- **A. Rename at the declaration site to something that says what it constrains** (as objectui#7324 did for its two), export it, and let `export *` carry it. Reversible, no behaviour change; the whole cost is choosing a name that does not collide.
- **B. Replace it with `@object-ui/types`' `ObjectSchemaMetadata`.** ⚠️ Measured on the `plugin-form` pair and **refused** there: that type requires `name` and requires a `type` on every field, so it NARROWS what such a function accepts rather than widening it. Re-measure here before assuming otherwise — the readers differ.
- **C. Leave it.** Every consumer keeps restating the shape.

Recommendation: **A**, for the same reason objectui#7324 landed on it — smallest reversible step, and B needs evidence this repo has not yet produced for this call site.
